notes: SHIP v1.14.427 - THE AISLE GIVES THE CONTEXT BACK TO WHOEVER LENT IT. Fixes a device-verify failure found by automating verify item 4 and CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE by the owner: 'rack is gone from build after close.' THE DEFECT. Opening the Forge aisle from Build correctly released Build's WebGL attachment - one live context is the iOS invariant and that part was never in question. Closing it never gave the context back. forge3d_close disposed the aisle and then called reh3d_activate3D, which restores the RACK-DETAIL surface and, by its own comment, is a no-op when no reh3dCanvasHost exists - exactly the case when the aisle was opened FROM BUILD. bw_mount3D has one caller, bw_render, so only a Build re-render could rebuild it, and nothing on the close path re-rendered Build. The IntersectionObserver could not cover it either: it pauses and RESUMES an existing attachment and cannot recreate a RELEASED one. Measured at 2.5s and again at 11s after close, well past Build's roughly 5s re-arm budget: bw-mount visible at a real 326x320 box, zero canvases, zero attachments. Build is the operational centre - the surface the shift runs from - so this was a silent blank in the worst possible place. THE FIX, AND WHY THIS SHAPE. The close path already TRIED to restore the surface it came from; it just only knew one address and called it unconditionally. So the aisle now records who it borrowed from. forge3d_open captures the active attachment BEFORE registration releases it - ordering is the whole mechanism, since releaseOthers has already destroyed the lender by the time the aisle is registered - and forge3d_close hands the context back to THAT surface. Attachments gained an optional reacquire callback: pause and resume operate on a LIVE attachment, and nothing could rebuild a released one, which is precisely the gap. The reacquire is generic, not a Build special case: rackElevation_render3D is the single renderer behind BOTH Build's bw-mount and the rack-detail host, so 'call the thing that built me with the arguments that built me' covers every rack surface and no caller needs to know it exists. A Build-shaped special case next to the rack-detail special case would only have guaranteed a third one later. Safe by construction: an attachment exists only because that render SUCCEEDED, so re-running it cannot land on the no-WebGL fallback path. THIS CANNOT REPRODUCE THE .405 CLASS. That defect was a Build re-arm stealing a LIVE context out from under the aisle. Here the aisle is disposed BEFORE the lender re-registers, so nothing is live at the moment of hand-back. The previous owner is also checked for DOM connection first: if its surface re-rendered while the aisle was open it has already re-mounted itself and is skipped. When no lender was captured - the aisle opened from a path holding no attachment - the pre-.427 reh3d_activate3D call is preserved exactly, so those paths are unchanged. MEASURED ACROSS TEN ROUND TRIPS, before and after. Before: openCanvases 5, openLive 1, closedCanvases 4, closedLive 0 - flat, every round. After: openCanvases 5, openLive 1, closedCanvases 5, closedLive 1 - flat, every round. The context comes home and STILL only one is ever live, so the hand-back did not buy correctness with a leak. THE LEAK QUESTION WAS ALREADY CLEAN and stays clean: round 10 is byte-identical to round 1 in both runs. TESTS. The x10 round-trip test in 02-build-forge.spec.js now asserts the context returns to rack:bw-mount on EVERY round. It previously asserted attachments.length <= 1 after close - which 0 satisfies - while the spec header claimed the round trip leaves Build intact. That tolerant bound is why five months of green suites never saw this: a bound that permits the defect reads as coverage. The hand-back test was pinned with test.fail() at v1.14.426 and flipped to 'Expected to fail, but passed' the moment this fix landed; the pin is removed rather than edited, because that flip is the proof. 02-build-forge and 08-forge-layout: 31 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4583/4583, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No UI surface changed. No parser change. ?legacy=1 unaffected - the single-context invariant was already deliberately ungated in both houses and this only changes what happens AFTER the aisle closes. DEVICE-VERIFY (verify item 4, re-run): from Build open the aisle, close it, and the Build rack preview must still show the rack - not an empty box. Repeat x10: no blank, no slowdown, and Build must have the rack every single time.
